data.name: Calixta
data.gender_notes: Calixta is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word calix, meaning 'chalice' or 'cup'. In Christian tradition, Calixta refers to the kind and self-sacrificing qualities of a woman who gives her all, like the cup used in the Eucharist. The name Calixta carries the meaning “Most Kind” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Calixta usually hope their child will grow to embody most kind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of selflessness and kindness.
data.etymology: Calixta belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Most Kind.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Calixta total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: קאליקסטה
in_hebrew.meaning: השם קאליקסטה נגזר מיוונית ופירושו יקרה ביותר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם קאליקסטה מקורו ביוונית ופירושו 'יקרה ביותר' או 'היקרה'. הוא קשור למונח היווני 'kalos', שפירושו יופי או טוב. השם משמש לעיתים קרובות בקהילות נוצריות ומשקף את הערך והחשיבות של השם ברוחניות הנוצרית. השימוש בשם זה מקושר גם למסורת של שמות יווניים-נוצריים.

in_greek.name: Καλήστα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Καλήστα προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'kalos', που σημαίνει ομορφιά ή καλό. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόμοιοι όροι χρησιμοποιούνται για να περιγράψουν πνευματική ομορφιά και αξία. Το όνομα Καλήστα αντικατοπτρίζει την πνευματική σημασία και την εκτίμηση της Εκκλησίας στην Παλιά και Νέα Διαθήκη.

in_latin.name: Calixta
in_latin.meaning: Calixta means most precious or beautiful
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Calixta is derived from the Greek term 'kalos', meaning beauty or good. In Latin Christianity, the name signifies spiritual beauty and preciousness. Historically, it has been used in various Christian cultures to denote someone cherished by God. The Latin adaptation retains the original Greek essence.

in_english.name: Calixta
in_english.meaning: Calixta means most precious or beautiful in a spiritual sense
in_english.long_meaning: The name Calixta originates from the Greek word 'kalos', meaning beauty or precious. It carries significant spiritual connotations in Christian traditions, symbolizing inner beauty and value in the eyes of God. Historically, the name has been associated with virtues of beauty and goodness. In modern Christian cultures, Calixta is chosen for its unique yet biblically rooted meaning.

data.cultural_impact: The name Calixta, though uncommon, carries connotations of strength, kindness, and self-sacrifice, which are values cherished in many cultures. The association with the Latin word 'calix' and the Christian symbolism connected with it adds a layer of sophistication and depth to the name.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian spirituality, Calixta represents a virtuous woman whose heart is full of love and generosity, like the chalice in the Last Supper. She is an embodiment of Christ’s teachings, giving freely of herself to others, providing comfort, encouragement, and strength, and offering her life in service to God and her community. Her name serves as a constant reminder of the spiritual journey towards greater selflessness, kindness, and compassion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Calixta, derived from the Latin name Calix, symbolizes the chalice or cup of the Eucharist, representing the deep spiritual connection and nourishment received through faith. Her name also suggests the virtues of patience and purity, reminding us to endure life's trials with calmness and grace.

historical_references.reference: In medieval Europe, Calixtus I (c. 330-372 AD) was a Pope of the Catholic Church who reigned from 371 to 372. He is considered the first Spanish Pope and played a significant role in the consolidation of papal power. Calixtus I is also known for his efforts to combat various heresies, including Donatism.

In the early modern period, the name Calixta was borne by Saint Calixta of Rome (d. 5th or 6th century AD), a virgin and martyr. Her exact historical details are not well-known, but she is venerated in the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches.
historical_references.context: Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches
